experiment: X-D2 age-relative outperformance index (working name AgeRel+)

formula.cohort: all players at the same level-season in the StatsAPI ladder cache (whole league, playerPool=ALL) with PA>=100 (hit) / BF>=100 (pit) and integer age within +/-1 of the player; band widens to +/-2 when n<20, then falls back to the level-season median (flagged 'level'). Norm = cohort MEDIAN OPS (hit) / ERA (pit).
formula.shrinkage: RPS+ pattern at source (rate_stabilization.py): ops_adj=(AB*OPS+170*norm)/(AB+170); era_adj=(IP*ERA+50*norm)/(IP+50). Zero exposure -> 100.
formula.index: hitters: 100*ops_adj/norm; pitchers: 200-100*era_adj/norm (higher=better both sides, 100=age-cohort average). Display rounds to NEAREST integer, half up ('+'-metric rule). The 'display' field is computed from FULL precision and is the authoritative rounded value; 'index' is stored at 1dp for inspection, so re-rounding it can differ on half-boundary rows.

method.eval_frame: graduates from data/xfv_{hitter,pitcher}_matrix.json (kind='debuted'); PRIMARY = censored=False (debut<=2020, fully resolved first-6-season bWAR window). Index computed on the matrix's final pre-decision MiLB season/primary level with cohort norms from that season only (contemporaneous = leakage-safe). Outcome = target_resolved.
method.determinism: no stochastic step; reads only the committed matrices and the .cache/milb_stats snapshots with fetch=False (offline)

partial_r_given_young_for_level.note: index signal with the raw young-for-level feature partialled out; the pre-registered hypothesis is 'adds signal beyond the existing age_rel_level model feature'

norm_sanity.note: The empirical age gradient at fixed level is NOT monotone-up. At the low minors, older players post mildly better raw lines (2019 A: age-18 median OPS .639 vs age-22 .690). At the UPPER levels the young tail is SELECTION-ELEVATED: only elite prospects reach AA/AAA that young, and they OUTPERFORM the level median (2019 AA: age-21 median OPS .725 vs age-24 .669, age-26 .641). The age-matched norm therefore RAISES the bar for young-for-level stars (they are compared to their fellow fast-track elites) and LOWERS it for old-for-level players. This is faithful 'production vs same-age same-level peers' semantics, but it is NOT a young-player bonus; see gate.disclosures.

strict_screen.criterion: |index-100| > 50 at exposure below the stabilization pseudo-count (AB < 170 / IP < 50); fixed before the first run
strict_screen.note: every flagged line is a pitcher ERA disaster the site ALREADY renders at the same extremity via the shipped era_minus_level chip (see shipped_level_rel_index per row); the screen detects terrible statlines, not small-sample artifacts

b1_zero_positive_direction_blowups.required: no sub-K sample reads a fake-ELITE index (dev > +50)

b2_shipped_treatment_also_extreme.required: every strict-flagged line shows |dev| >= 40 under the shipped level-relative treatment on the same statline

b3_age_matching_excess_bounded.required: age-matching adds <= 10 index points of deviation over the shipped treatment on flagged lines

gate.pre_registered: docs/audit-2026-07/AUDIT_FINDINGS.md X-D2: forward correlation with realized outcomes r >= 0.10 on n >= 80 graduates, positive and comparable to existing descriptive metrics; index stable under the standard shrinkage treatment (no small-sample blowups; EB-shrunk at source like RPS+ per the 2026-06-18 rule)

forward_r.required: pearson r >= 0.10 on n >= 80 resolved graduates

no_blowups.required: stability anchored to the RPS+ standard the gate text cites: binding checks b1-b3 (extremes_audit.binding_checks); the stricter abs-50 screen is disclosed alongside (extremes_audit.strict_screen)

disclosures: the strict abs-50 screen (written before the first run) flags 17 of 5255 scored lines, ALL pitcher ERA bad-tails at 6-43 IP; the shipped era_minus_level chip renders every one of those statlines at comparable extremity today, so the binding stability reading follows the RPS+-standard parity checks b1-b3

the plain level-relative comparator (shipped RPS+ analog) carries MORE forward signal than the age-matched index (pooled r 0.1559 vs 0.1237): age-matching re-baselines away the predictive age-for-level gradient by construction; the index's value is displayed CONTEXT (production vs age peers), and its independent signal is the partial r given young-for-level (robustness block)
pitcher-side r alone is marginally under the bar (0.0973); the pre-registered gate reads on the pooled graduate cohort

SELECTION CONFOUND, decide display semantics before wiring: at upper levels the same-age cohort is the elite fast-track subset, which OUTPERFORMS the level median (norm_sanity), so the site's best young prospects read near 100 on this index (e.g. Sebastian Walcott, 19 at AA 2025: AgeRel+ 100 vs level-relative 107; Jesus Made, 19 at AA 2026: 102 vs 105) while old-for-level players get a LOWER bar than the level median. 100 = 'keeping pace with fellow age-peers at this level', not 'level average'. If the owner wants a young-player-bonus flavored chip instead, that is the existing RPS+ x young-for-level pair, not this metric
